title: Require Service Router Authorship
forbids: a named router leaf whose filename, sole runtime export, and configured module descendant disagree; an export alias except the language-required binding for a reserved public name; a detached callable that displaces operation authorship from an inline native effect or handler; operation authorship in a service-root or module-root router composition face; or a module-root router that imports outside direct local named router leaves and type-only contracts or exports anything except one plain router object
why: Handlers are the operation authoring sites: they consume the configured module context and perform the transition where oRPC owns the boundary. Filename-to-descendant alignment keeps a standalone operation or cohesive group on its declared module branch, while one module-root router.ts keeps public composition visible without acquiring behavior or creating a second index face.
remediate: Author each operation directly inside an inline effect(...) or handler(...) callback in modules/<module>/router/<name>.router.ts. Export only the matching lower-camel <name> value and author every operation in that file from module.<name> or its descendants. Use `<name>Operation` exported as `<name>` only when the public name is an ECMAScript reserved word. Move reusable decisions to qualified model policy and keep outside calls on context-provided ports. Import completed named router values into module-root router.ts and export one plain router object; do not add router/index.ts, runtime helpers, middleware, or procedure authorship there.
message: Named router leaves author operations; module-root router.ts only composes them.
